questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block takes $t$ time to slide down a plane inclined at $45°$ to the horizontal. If the surface is made smooth (frictionless), the block takes time $\dfrac{t}{2}$ to slide down the plane. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inclined plane is $\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{100}\right)$. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.solution:
Let the length of the inclined plane be $s$.

For the smooth inclined plane, the acceleration of the block is $a_1 = g \sin \theta$.

The time taken is $t_1 = \dfrac{t}{2}$. Using the second equation of motion $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} (g \sin \theta) \left(\dfrac{t}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{8} g \sin \theta t^2$

For the rough inclined plane, the acceleration of the block is $a_2 = g(\sin \theta - \mu \cos \theta)$.

The time taken is $t_2 = t$. Using the equation of motion again:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} g(\sin \theta - \mu \cos \theta) t^2$

Equating the two expressions for $s$:

$\dfrac{1}{8} g \sin \theta t^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} g(\sin \theta - \mu \cos \theta) t^2$

$\dfrac{1}{4} \sin \theta = \sin \theta - \mu \cos \theta$

Given $\theta = 45^{\circ}$, we have $\sin 45^{\circ} = \cos 45^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. Substituting these values:

$\dfrac{1}{4} = 1 - \mu$

$\mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$

We are given $\mu = \dfrac{\alpha}{100}$.

$\dfrac{\alpha}{100} = 0.75 \Rightarrow \alpha = 75$

Answer: $75$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two blocks ($P$ and $Q$) with respectively masses $2$ kg and $1.5$ kg are joined by a massless thread. These blocks are mounted on a frictionless pulley which is fixed on the edge of a cube ($S$), as shown in the figure below. Block $P$ is positioned on the top surface which has no friction and block $Q$ is in contact with side-surface, having coefficient friction $\mu$. The cube ($S$) moves towards the right with acceleration of $\dfrac{g}{2}$, where $g$ is gravitational acceleration. During this movement the block $P$ and $Q$ remain stationary. The value of $\mu$ is _______. (take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Let us analyze the forces acting on blocks $P$ and $Q$ in the non-inertial frame of reference of the cube $S$, which is moving to the right with an acceleration $a = \dfrac{g}{2} = 5 \text{ m/s}^2$.

In this frame, a pseudo force acts on both blocks towards the left.

For block $P$ (mass $m_P = 2 \text{ kg}$):
The forces in the horizontal direction are the tension $T$ in the string (acting towards the right) and the pseudo force $F_{pP}$ (acting towards the left). Since block $P$ is stationary relative to the cube and there is no friction on the top surface:
$T = m_P a = 2 \times 5 = 10 \text{ N}$

For block $Q$ (mass $m_Q = 1.5 \text{ kg}$):
The horizontal forces are the normal reaction $N$ from the side surface of the cube (acting towards the right) and the pseudo force $F_{pQ}$ (acting towards the left). Since block $Q$ is stationary horizontally relative to the cube:
$N = m_Q a = 1.5 \times 5 = 7.5 \text{ N}$

The vertical forces acting on block $Q$ are the downward gravitational force $m_Q g$, the upward tension $T$, and the frictional force $f$.
The downward force is $m_Q g = 1.5 \times 10 = 15 \text{ N}$.
Since $m_Q g > T$ ($15 \text{ N} > 10 \text{ N}$), the block has a tendency to slide downwards, so the static friction $f$ must act upwards.
For vertical equilibrium of block $Q$:
$T + f = m_Q g$
$10 + f = 15 \Rightarrow f = 5 \text{ N}$

To keep the block stationary, the required friction must be less than or equal to the maximum static friction ($f \le \mu N$). Assuming the limiting case to find the value of $\mu$:
$\mu N = f$
$\mu (7.5) = 5$
$\mu = \dfrac{5}{7.5} = \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.67$

Answer: $0.67$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass of $1\text{ kg}$ is kept on an inclined plane with $30°$ inclination with respect to horizontal plane and it is at rest initially. Then the whole assembly is moved up with constant velocity of $4\text{ m/s}$. The work done by the frictional force in time $2\text{ s}$ is _______ J. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Since the assembly moves with a constant velocity, the acceleration of the mass is zero. The mass is in equilibrium relative to the incline.

The frictional force $f$ acting on the mass balances the component of gravity along the inclined plane. Therefore, the magnitude of the frictional force is:

$f = mg \sin 30^\circ$

Substituting the given values ($m = 1\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):

$f = 1 \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 5\text{ N}$

The direction of the frictional force is upwards along the incline. Since the incline makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal, the frictional force makes an angle of $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$ with the vertical upward direction.

The displacement $s$ of the assembly in time $t = 2\text{ s}$ is vertically upwards:

$s = vt = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ m}$

The work done by the frictional force is:

$W = f s \cos 60^\circ$

$W = 5 \times 8 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 20\text{ J}$

Answer: $20$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Three masses $m_1 = 4$ kg, $m_2 = 4$ kg and $m_3 = 6$ kg are suspended from a fixed smooth frictionless pulley as shown in the figure below. The value of $T_1/T_2$ is _____.
(take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Let the acceleration of the system be $a$. The total mass on the right side is $m_2 + m_3 = 4 + 6 = 10$ kg, and the mass on the left side is $m_1 = 4$ kg. Since $10$ kg $> 4$ kg, the right side accelerates downwards and the left side accelerates upwards.

The common acceleration $a$ of the system is given by:
$a = \dfrac{(m_2 + m_3) - m_1}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} g$
$a = \dfrac{10 - 4}{4 + 4 + 6} g = \dfrac{6}{14} g = \dfrac{3}{7} g$

For mass $m_1$, the equation of motion is:
$T_1 - m_1 g = m_1 a$
$T_1 = m_1(g + a) = 4 \left(g + \dfrac{3}{7}g\right) = 4 \left(\dfrac{10}{7}g\right) = \dfrac{40}{7}g$

For mass $m_3$, the equation of motion is:
$m_3 g - T_2 = m_3 a$
$T_2 = m_3(g - a) = 6 \left(g - \dfrac{3}{7}g\right) = 6 \left(\dfrac{4}{7}g\right) = \dfrac{24}{7}g$

The ratio of the tensions is:
$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{40}{7}g}{\dfrac{24}{7}g} = \dfrac{40}{24} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

Answer: $5/3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A wedge $Y$ with mass of $10$ kg and all frictionless surfaces and the inclined surface making $37°$ with horizontal. A block $X$ with mass $2$ kg is placed at the highest point of the wedge as shown in figure is at rest. At $t = 0$ wedge $(Y)$ is pulled toward right with constant force $(f)$ of $24$ N. Taking the block $X$ at rest at $t = 0$, the time taken by it to slide down $8.8$ m on the slope, while $Y$ is on the move, is _____ s.
(take $\tan(37°) = 3/4$ and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Horizontal acceleration of the wedge (assuming the block and wedge move together horizontally):
$A = \dfrac{f}{M + m} = \dfrac{24}{10 + 2} = 2\text{ m/s}^2$

Working in the non-inertial frame of the wedge, the block experiences a pseudo force $mA$ directed opposite to the wedge's acceleration. The components along the incline are:
Component of gravity down the incline: $g\sin 37^\circ$
Component of pseudo force up the incline: $A\cos 37^\circ$

Net relative acceleration of the block down the incline:
$a_{\text{rel}} = g\sin 37^\circ - A\cos 37^\circ$

Using $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$ and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$:
$a_{\text{rel}} = 10(0.6) - 2(0.8) = 6 - 1.6 = 4.4\text{ m/s}^2$

Time taken to slide a distance of $8.8\text{ m}$ along the incline, starting from rest:
$s = \dfrac{1}{2} a_{\text{rel}}\, t^2$

$8.8 = \dfrac{1}{2}(4.4)\,t^2$

$8.8 = 2.2\,t^2$

$t^2 = 4 \Rightarrow t = 2\text{ s}$

Hence, the required time is $2\text{ s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At $t=0$, a body of mass $100$ g starts moving under the influence of a force $(5\hat{i}+10\hat{j})$ N. After $2$ s its position is $(2x\hat{i}+5y\hat{j})$ m. The ratio $x:y$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Mass $m = 100 \text{ g} = 0.1 \text{ kg}$

Force $\vec{F} = 5\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} \text{ N}$

Acceleration $\vec{a} = \dfrac{\vec{F}}{m} = \dfrac{5\hat{i} + 10\hat{j}}{0.1} = 50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j} \text{ m/s}^2$

Since the body starts from rest, initial velocity $\vec{u} = 0$.

Position after $t = 2 \text{ s}$ is given by $\vec{r} = \vec{u}t + \dfrac{1}{2}\vec{a}t^2$

$\vec{r} = \dfrac{1}{2}(50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j})(2)^2 = 100\hat{i} + 200\hat{j} \text{ m}$

Comparing with the given position $\vec{r} = 2x\hat{i} + 5y\hat{j}$:

$2x = 100 \Rightarrow x = 50$

$5y = 200 \Rightarrow y = 40$

The ratio $x:y = 50:40 = 5:4$

Answer: $5:4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time taken by a block of mass $m$ to slide down from the highest point to the lowest point on a rough inclined plane is $50\%$ more compared to the time taken by the same block on identical inclined smooth plane. Both inclined planes are at $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the rough inclined surface and block is _____.
questions.solution:
Let the length of the inclined plane be $s$.

For the smooth inclined plane, the acceleration of the block is $a_1 = g \sin \theta$.

The time taken to slide down is $t_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a_1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{g \sin \theta}}$.

For the rough inclined plane, the acceleration of the block is $a_2 = g \sin \theta - \mu_k g \cos \theta$.

The time taken to slide down is $t_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a_2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{g (\sin \theta - \mu_k \cos \theta)}}$.

Given that $t_2$ is $50\%$ more than $t_1$, we have $t_2 = t_1 + 0.5 t_1 = \dfrac{3}{2} t_1$.

Squaring both sides gives $t_2^2 = \dfrac{9}{4} t_1^2$.

Substituting the expressions for $t_1^2$ and $t_2^2$:

$\dfrac{2s}{g (\sin \theta - \mu_k \cos \theta)} = \dfrac{9}{4} \left( \dfrac{2s}{g \sin \theta} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\sin \theta - \mu_k \cos \theta} = \dfrac{9}{4 \sin \theta}$

$4 \sin \theta = 9 \sin \theta - 9 \mu_k \cos \theta$

$9 \mu_k \cos \theta = 5 \sin \theta$

$\mu_k = \dfrac{5}{9} \tan \theta$

Given $\theta = 45^\circ$, we have $\tan 45^\circ = 1$.

$\mu_k = \dfrac{5}{9} \times 1 = \dfrac{5}{9}$

Answer: $5/9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $0.5$ kg mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius $4$ m rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall (without falling) is $5$ rad/s. The coefficient of friction between the drum's inner wall surface and mass is _______. (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
The normal force $N$ provides the necessary centripetal force for the mass to move in a circle:

$N = m \omega^2 R$

For the mass to remain stuck to the wall without falling, the upward frictional force must balance the downward gravitational force:

$f \ge mg$

Since the maximum static friction is $f_{max} = \mu N$, we have:

$\mu N \ge mg$

$\mu (m \omega^2 R) \ge mg$

$\mu \ge \dfrac{g}{\omega^2 R}$

Substituting the given values $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, $\omega = 5$ rad/s, and $R = 4$ m:

$\mu \ge \dfrac{10}{5^2 \times 4}$

$\mu \ge \dfrac{10}{100}$

$\mu \ge 0.1$

The minimum coefficient of friction is $0.1$.

Answer: $0.1$

Since the maximum static friction is $f_{max} = \mu N$, we have:

$\mu N \ge mg$

$\mu (m \omega^2 R) \ge mg$

$\mu \ge \dfrac{g}{\omega^2 R}$

Substituting the given values $g = 10$ m/s$^2$, $\omega = 5$ rad/s, and $R = 4$ m:

$\mu \ge \dfrac{10}{5^2 \times 4}$

$\mu \ge \dfrac{10}{100}$

$\mu \ge 0.1$

The minimum coefficient of friction is $0.1$.

Answer: $0.1$

questions.q: A small block of mass $m$ slides down from the top of a frictionless inclined surface, while the inclined plane is moving towards left with constant acceleration $a_{0}$. The angle between the inclined plane and ground is $\theta$ and its base length is $L$. Assuming that initially the small block is at the top of the inclined plane, the time it takes to reach the lowest point of the inclined plane is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
$mg\sin\theta - ma_0\cos\theta = ma$
$a = g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta$
Now using,
$S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}a_{down}t^2$
$\dfrac{L}{\cos\theta} = \dfrac{1}{2}(g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta)t^2$
$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2L}{g\sin\theta\cos\theta - a_0\cos^2\theta}}$
$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{4L}{g\sin 2\theta - a_0(1 + \cos 2\theta)}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ falls from rest through a resistive medium having resistive force, $F=-k v$, where $v$ is the velocity of the particle and $k$ is a constant. Which of the following graphs represents velocity ($v$) versus time ($t$)?
questions.solution:
The particle experiences downward gravitational force (mg) and upward resistive force (-kv).
The equation of motion is $m\frac{dv}{dt} = mg - kv$.
Initially at $t=0$, $v=0$ gives maximum acceleration $a_0 = g$.
As velocity increases, the resistive force increases, reducing the net acceleration.
Eventually the particle reaches terminal velocity $v_t = \frac{mg}{k}$ when acceleration becomes zero.
The velocity-time graph shows an increasing curve starting from origin with decreasing slope, asymptotically approaching the terminal velocity.
This behavior matches option (1), which displays a curve starting at (0,0) with steep initial slope that gradually flattens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A block of mass 5 kg is moving on an inclined plane which makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. Friction coefficient between the block and inclined plane surface is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. The force to be applied on the block so that the block will move down without acceleration is $\_\_\_\_$ N.
$\left(g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$.
questions.solution:
For motion without acceleration, net force = 0.
Component of weight along incline: $mg\sin(30°) = 5 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 25$ N (down).
Normal force: $N = mg\cos(30°) = 50 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 25\sqrt{3}$ N.
Friction force opposing downward motion:
$f = \mu N = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 25\sqrt{3} = 37.5$ N (up).
For equilibrium along the incline, applying force F down the incline:
$mg\sin\theta + F = f$, so $25 + F = 37.5$, giving $F = 12.5$ N.

questions.q: A flexible chain of mass $m$ hangs between two fixed points at the same level. The inclination of the chain with the horizontal at the two points of support is $30^{\circ}$. Considering the equilibrium of each half of the chain, the tension of the chain at the lowest point is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
A chain of mass $m$ hangs between two fixed points at the same level with inclination $30°$ at support points.
Consider equilibrium of one half of the chain (mass $m/2$):
Horizontal equilibrium: $T_0 = T_1\cos(30°) = T_1 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
Vertical equilibrium: $T_1\sin(30°) = \frac{m}{2}g$
From vertical equation: $T_1 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{mg}{2}$, giving $T_1 = mg$
Substituting into horizontal equation: $T_0 = mg \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}mg$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring of force constant $15 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ is cut into two pieces. If the ratio of their length is $1: 3$, then the force constant of smaller piece is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}$.
questions.solution:
Spring force constant is inversely proportional to length: $k \propto \frac{1}{L}$
So $kL = $ constant for a given spring material and structure.
Original spring: $k = 15$ N/m, length $= L$.
Smaller piece has length $\frac{L}{4}$ (since length ratio is 1:3, smaller is $\frac{1}{4}$ of total).
For smaller piece: $k_1 \times \frac{L}{4} = 15 \times L$
$k_1 = 15 \times 4 = 60$ N/m

questions.q:
In the given figure the blocks $A, B$ and $C$ weigh $4 \mathrm{~kg}, 6 \mathrm{~kg}$ and 8 kg respectively. The co-efficient of sliding friction between any two surfaces is 0.5. The force $\vec{F}$ required to slide the block $C$ with constant speed is $\_\_\_\_$ N.
(Use $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
For the 8 kg block (C) to move with constant velocity, $F_{net} = 0$.

Friction forces acting:
- Between C and ground: $f = \mu(m_A + m_B + m_C)g = 0.5 \times (4+6+8) \times 10 = 90$ N
- Between C and B: $f = \mu(m_A + m_B)g = 0.5 \times (4+6) \times 10 = 50$ N

For the 6 kg block (B):
$T = f_{\text{B on ground}} + f_{\text{A on B}}$
$T = \mu(m_A + m_B)g \cdot \frac{m_B}{m_A+m_B} + \mu \cdot m_A \cdot g$
$T = 20 + 50 = 70$ N

For the 8 kg block (C):
$F = 90 + T + 50 = 90 + 70 + 50 = 210$ N

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A large drum having radius $R$ is spinning around its axis with angular velocity $\omega$, as shown in figure. The minimum value of $\omega$ so that a body of mass $M$ remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass $M$ as $\mu$, is :
questions.solution:
Consider the mass $M$ in the frame of the rotating drum. The forces acting on the mass are:
1. Weight $Mg$ acting vertically downwards.
2. Normal reaction $N$ from the wall acting towards the center, which provides the centripetal force: $N = M\omega^2 R$.
3. Frictional force $f$ acting vertically upwards to balance the weight.
For the mass to remain stuck to the wall, the frictional force must balance the weight: $f = Mg$.
The maximum available static friction is $f_{max} = \mu N = \mu M\omega^2 R$.
To prevent slipping, we must have $f_{max} \ge Mg$.
$\mu M\omega^2 R \ge Mg$
$\omega^2 \ge \frac{g}{\mu R}$
$\omega \ge \sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu R}}$
The minimum value of $\omega$ is $\sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu R}}$.

questions.q: A 4 kg mass moves under the influence of a force $\vec{F}=\left(4 t^{3} \hat{i}-3 t \hat{j}\right) \mathrm{N}$ where $t$ is the time in second. If mass starts from origin at $t=0$, the velocity and position after $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ will be:

Given $\vec{F} = (4t^3\hat{i} - 3t\hat{j})$ N, m = 4 kg
$\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m} = t^3\hat{i} - \frac{3t}{4}\hat{j}$
Integrating with $\vec{v}(0) = 0$:
$\vec{v} = \frac{t^4}{4}\hat{i} - \frac{3t^2}{8}\hat{j}$
At $t = 2$: $\vec{v} = \frac{16}{4}\hat{i} - \frac{12}{8}\hat{j} = 4\hat{i} - \frac{3}{2}\hat{j}$
Integrating with $\vec{r}(0) = 0$:
$\vec{r} = \frac{t^5}{20}\hat{i} - \frac{t^3}{8}\hat{j}$
At $t = 2$: $\vec{r} = \frac{32}{20}\hat{i} - \frac{8}{8}\hat{j} = \frac{8}{5}\hat{i} - \hat{j}$

The magnitude of $F$ is : (Assume that the system is in equilibrium and $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1 \sin 45^{\circ}=\mathrm{F} \\ & \mathrm{T}_1 \cos 45^{\circ}=\mathrm{T}_2=1 \times \mathrm{g} \\ & \therefore \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{F}=10 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A given object takes $\mathrm{n}$ times the time to slide down $45^{\circ}$ rough inclined plane as it takes the time to slide down an identical perfectly smooth $45^{\circ}$ inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of inclined plane is :
questions.solution: Case-1 : No friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta) \mathrm{t}_1^2 \\ & \mathrm{t}_1=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \end{aligned}$ Case-2 : With friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta) \mathrm{t}_2^2 \\ & \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu g \cos \theta}}=\mathrm{n} \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \\ & \mu=1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^2} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A car of $800 \mathrm{~kg}$ is taking turn on a banked road of radius $300 \mathrm{~m}$ and angle of banking $30^{\circ}$. If coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely: $\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \sqrt{3}=1.73\right)$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=800 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{r}=300 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \theta=30^{\circ} \\ & \mu_{\mathrm{s}}=0.2 \\ & \mathrm{~V}_{\max }=\sqrt{\operatorname{Rg}\left[\frac{\tan \theta+\mu}{1-\mu \tan \theta}\right]} \\ & =\sqrt{300 \times \mathrm{g} \times\left[\frac{\tan 30^{\circ}+0.2}{1-0.2 \times \tan 30^{\circ}}\right]} \\ & =\sqrt{300 \times 10 \times\left[\frac{0.57+0.2}{1-0.2 \times 0.57}\right]} \\ & \mathrm{V}_{\max }=51.4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A block of mass $5kg$ is placed on a rough inclined surface as shown in the figure. If $\overset{\to}{F}1$ is the force required to just move the block up the inclined plane and $\overset{\to}{F}2$ is the force required to just prevent the block from sliding down, then the value of $\left|\overset{\to}{F}1\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{F}2\right| is: [Use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$]

$
questions.solution:
Limiting friction force is, ${f}_{max} = \mu\left(mgcos\theta\right)$

$= 0 .1 \times \dfrac{50 \times \sqrt{3}}{2}$

$= 2 .5 \sqrt{3}N$

For first case:

We can write, ${F}_{1} = mgsin\theta + {f}_{max}$

$= 25 + 2 .5 \sqrt{3}$

For second case:

${F}_{2} = mgsin\theta - {f}_{max}$

$= 25 - 2 .5 \sqrt{3}$

$∴ {F}_{1} - {F}_{2} = 5\sqrt{3}N$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coin is placed on a disc. The coefficient of friction between the coin and the disc is $\mu$. If the distance of the coin from the center of the disc is $r$, the maximum angular velocity which can be given to the disc, so that the coin does not slip away, is :
questions.solution:
Normal force acting on the coin is, $N = mg$.

Required friction force to provide centripetal force for the coin is, $f = m{\omega}^{2}r$ and maximum value of static friction force available is, $f = \muN = \mumg$.

For limiting condition, we can write

$⇒ \mumg = mr{\omega}^{2}$

$⇒ \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mug}{r}}$

questions.q: A block of mass $m$ is placed on a surface having vertical cross section given by $y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4}$. If coefficient of friction is $0 . 5$, the maximum height above the ground at which block can be placed without slipping is:
questions.solution:
At equilibrium, $tan\theta = \mu$.

Now, $tan\theta$ is slope of the curve. Therefore,

$tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{2}$

Now, 

$\dfrac{x}{2} = 0 . 5 ⇒ x = 1$

Required height 

$y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}m$.

questions.q: A stone of mass $900g$ is tied to a string and moved in a vertical circle of radius $1m$ making $10rpm$. The tension in the string, when the stone is at the lowest point is (if ${\pi}^{2} = 9 . 8$ and $g = 9 . 8m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Given that 

Given the mass $m = 900g = \dfrac{900}{1000}kg = \dfrac{9}{10}kg$,

The radius of the circular path $r = 1m$

And, the angular velocity

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi N}{60} = \dfrac{2\pi ( 10 )}{60} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}rad{s}^{- 1}$

With reference to the above diagram, the formula to calculate the tension at the lowermost point can be written as

$T - mg = mr{\omega}^{2} ⇒ T = mg + mr{\omega}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\begin{cases}T & = & \dfrac{9}{10} \times 9 . 8 + \dfrac{9}{10} \times 1{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}^{2} \\ & = & 8 . 82 + \dfrac{9}{10} \times \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{9} \\ & = & 8 . 82 + 0 . 98 \\ & = & 9 . 8N\end{cases}$

questions.q: A particle is moving in a circle of radius $50cm$ in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of its acceleration are equal. If its speed at $t = 0$ is $4m{s}^{- 1}$, the time taken to complete the first revolution will be $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}\left[1 - {e}^{- 2\pi}\right]s$, where $\alpha =$______.
questions.solution:
Given:

$\left|\overset{\to}{a}c\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a}t\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{r} = \dfrac{dv}{dt}$

$⇒ {∫}_{4}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{{v}^{2}} = {∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{r}$

$⇒ {\left[\dfrac{- 1}{v}\right]}_{4}^{v} = \dfrac{t}{r}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{4} = 2t$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{4}{1 - 8t} = \dfrac{ds}{dt}$

$⇒ 4{∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{1 - 8t} = {∫}_{0}^{s}ds$

$\left(r = 0 . 5m, \text{distance}\text{covered}s = 2\pir = \pi\right)$

$⇒ 4 \times \dfrac{[ ln ( 1 - 8t ) {]}_{0}^{t}}{- 8} = \pi$

$⇒ ℓn ( 1 - 8t ) = - 2\pi$

$⇒ 1 - 8t = {e}^{- 2\pi}$

$⇒ t = \left(1 - {e}^{- 2\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{8}s$

So, $\alpha = 8$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The limiting force of static friction depends on the area of contact and independent of materials.
Statement (II) : The limiting force of kinetic friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on materials.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.solution:
The limiting force of static friction depends on both the normal force and the coefficient of static friction, but it does not depend on the area of contact.

The force of kinetic friction is indeed dependent on the nature of the materials in contact and the normal force, but not on the area of contact.

Hence, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.solution:
For the train, moving along the curved rails, it can be written, with reference to the figure below, that

$tan\theta = \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{Rg} . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, from the above figure, it follows that

$tan\theta = \dfrac{h}{1 . 5} . . . \left(2\right)$

questions.q: The position vector of a particle related to time $t$ is given by $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(10t\overset{^}{i} + 15{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)m$. The direction of net force experienced by the particle is :
questions.solution:
Given, the position vector of the particle is

$\overset{\to}{r} = 10t\overset{^}{i} + 15{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

The velocity of the particle can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{v} & = & \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{r}}{dt} \\ & = & \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(10t\overset{^}{i} + 15{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right) \\ & = & 10\overset{^}{i} + 30t\overset{^}{j}\end{cases}$

And, the acceleration of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & = & \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt} \\ & = & \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(10\overset{^}{i} + 30t\overset{^}{j}\right) \\ & = & 30\overset{^}{j}\end{cases}$

Hence, the force on the particle can be written as

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{F} & = & m\overset{\to}{a} \\ & = & 30m\overset{^}{j}\end{cases}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass $500g$ moves along $x$-axis such that it's velocity varies with displacement $x$ according to the relation $v = 10\sqrt{x}m{s}^{- 1}$ the force acting on the body is:
questions.solution:
It is given that

$v = 10\sqrt{x}m{s}^{- 1}$

Force is defined by $F = m\dfrac{dv}{dt} . . . ( i )$

Multiplying and dividing equation (i) by $dx$

$F = m\dfrac{dv}{dt}\dfrac{dx}{dx} ⇒ F = m\dfrac{dx}{dt}\dfrac{dv}{dx} = mv\dfrac{dv}{dx} . . . ( ii )$

Finding the values of the terms in equation (ii)
$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{10}{2\sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{x}}$
$v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = a = 10\sqrt{x} \times \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{x}} = 50m{s}^{- 2}$

Hence, the force is
$F = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 50 = 25N$.

questions.q: A coin placed on a rotating table just slips when it is placed at a distance of $1cm$ from the centre. If the angular velocity of the table is halved, it will just slip when placed at a distance of _____ from the centre:
questions.solution:
The coin will slip when

$\mumg = m{\omega}^{2}r$

$⇒ \mug = {\omega}^{2} \times 1cm . . . ( i )$

Now, $\omega ' = \dfrac{\omega}{2}$

$\mug = {\left(\dfrac{\omega}{2}\right)}^{2}R . . . ( ii )$

Hence we can write from (i) and (ii)

${\omega}^{2} \times 1cm = \dfrac{{\omega}^{2}}{4}R ⇒ R = 4cm$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : An electric fan continues to rotate for some time after the current is switched off.

Reason R: Fan continues to rotate due to inertia of motion.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
questions.solution:
When a fan is rotating, it acquires some kinetic energy. When the switch is off, because of its motion, it continues rotating for some time until it stops because of the air friction. So it is due to inertia of motion that fan continues to rotate.

Hence, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution:
The equation for velocity is

$\overset{\to}{v} = \left(2t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

Thus, the acceleration is

$\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt} = \dfrac{d ( 2t\overset{^}{i} + 3{t}^{2}\overset{^}{j} )}{dt} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 6t\overset{^}{j}\right)$

At $t = 1s$, $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}$

The force is written as $\overset{\to}{F} = m\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}}{2} = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

Comparing it with the given value of force, $x = 3$.

questions.solution:
For the given combination, if the block is displaced towards right, elongation in one spring will be equal to the compression in other and the direction of force due to both spring will be the same and restoring in nature. Hence, both springs are effectively in parallel combination.

questions.solution:
Centripetal force will be provided by the spring force. Let the elongation in the spring be $x$, then we can write

$⇒ kx = m{\omega}^{2} ( r + x )$

$⇒ 7 . 5x = 2 . 5 ( 0 . 2 + x )$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{0 . 5}{5} = 0 . 1$

Therefore, required tension will be$T = kx = 0 . 75N$.

The free body diagram for the given scenario is shown below-

From the equilibrium of the vertical component of forces, it can be written that

$\begin{cases}N & = & mg - Fsin30 ° \\ & = & mg - \dfrac{F}{2} \\ & = & 100 - \dfrac{F}{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{200 - F}{2} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )\end{cases}$

Substitute the expression for the normal reaction force from equation (1) into equation (2) and solve to calculate the value of the applied force.

$\begin{cases}\sqrt{3}\dfrac{F}{2} & = & 0 . 25 \times \left(\dfrac{200 - F}{2}\right) \\ 4\sqrt{3}F & = & 200 - F \\ F & = & \dfrac{200}{4\sqrt{3} + 1} \\ & \approx & 25 . 2\end{cases}$

questions.q: A block of mass $5kg$ is placed at rest on a table of rough surface. Now, if a force of $30N$ is applied in the direction parallel to surface of the table, the block slides through a distance of $50m$ in an interval of time $10s$. Coefficient of kinetic friction is (given, $g = 10m{s}^{– 2}$ ):
questions.solution:
Forces acting on block is shown below

From the second equation of motion,

$s = \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2} ⇒ 50 = \dfrac{1}{2}a \times {10}^{2} ⇒ a = 1m{s}^{- 2}$

Applying Newton's second law in vertical direction,

$R - mg = 0 ⇒ R = mg$

(where $R$ is the magnitude of normal reaction on the block due to the surface)

If $\mu$ is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface, applying Newton's second law in horizontal direction,

$30 - \muR = ma ⇒ 30 - \mumg = ma ⇒ 30 - 50\mu = 5 ⇒ \mu = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0 . 5$

questions.q: A body of mass $10kg$ is moving with an initial speed of $20m{s}^{- 1}$. The body stops after $5s$ due to friction between body and the floor. The value of the coefficient of friction is: (Take acceleration due to gravity $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Friction force wil act opposite to the motion of the body.

$F = \muN = \mumg$

$⇒ a = - \mug\left(\text{-ve sign for direction relative to the motion of body}\right)$

Now, applying equation of motion, we get

$v = u + at$

$⇒ 0 = 20 + \left(- \mu \times 10\right) \times 5$

$⇒ 50\mu = 20$

$⇒ \mu = 0 . 4$

questions.q: The time taken by an object to slide down $45 °$ rough inclined plane is $n$ times as it takes to slide down a perfectly smooth $45 °$ incline plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the incline plane is:
questions.solution:
Let angle of inclination is $\theta = 45 °$.

Then, acceleration along the incline in case of smooth incline will be, ${a}_{1} = gsin\theta = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}$.

In case of rough incline, kinetic friction will act against the direction of motion. Normal force acting on the object will be $mgcos\theta$. Therefore, acceleration along the incline in case of rough incline will be,

${a}_{2} = gsin\theta - \mugcos\theta = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{\mug}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Now as per question,

${t}_{2} = n{t}_{1}$

and as the displacement covered is the same in both case, $0 + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{t}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}{t}_{1}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{\mug}{\sqrt{2}}\right){n}^{2}{t}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ \mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}$

questions.q: Force acts for $20s$ on a body of mass $20kg$, starting from rest, after which the force ceases and then body describes $50m$ in the next $10s$. The value of force will be :

For the second case when body is moving with constant velocity, we can write

$V = 0 + a \times 20$

$⇒ 5 = a \times 20$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{4}m{s}^{- 2}$

Hence, required force will be

$F = ma = 20 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 5N$

questions.q: A block of mass $m$ slides down the plane inclined at angle $30 °$ with an acceleration $\dfrac{g}{4}$ . The value of coefficient of kinetic friction will be :
questions.solution:
Applying Newton's second law along the direction perpendicular to inlined plane:

$N - mgcos{30}^{∘} = 0$ (As $\theta = 30 °$)

(since the acceleration of block in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane is $0$)

$∴ N = mgcos{30}^{∘}$ .....(1)

Let $\mu$ be the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the inclined plane. Applying Newton's second law along inclined plane:

$mgsin{30}^{∘} - \muN = ma = m\dfrac{g}{4}$ ....(2)

(since the acceleration along the inclined plane, $a = \dfrac{g}{4}$)

$∴ mgsin{30}^{∘} - \mumgcos{30}^{∘} = m\dfrac{g}{4}$ (from equation 1 and 2)

$⇒ \dfrac{mg}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mumg = m\dfrac{g}{4}$

$⇒$\mu = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q:
Consider a block kept on an inclined plane (inclined at $45 °$) as shown in the figure. If the force required to just push it up the incline is $2$ times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down, the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane $( µ )$ is equal to :

.
questions.solution:
The forces acting on block is shown in above figure.

Here, normal force, $N = mgcos45 °$ and frictional force, $f = \muN$.

Balancing the force along incline, we have

${F}_{1} = mgsin45 ° + f = mgsin45 ° + \muN$

$⇒ {F}_{1} = \dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}} + \mumgcos45 °$

$⇒ {F}_{1} = \dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}\left(1 + \mu\right)$

Now, the forces acting on block to just push it up on inclined plane is shown below.

Balancing the force along incline, we have

${F}_{2} = mgsin45 ° - f = mgsin45 ° - \muN$

$= \dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}\left(1 - \mu\right)$

Given, ${F}_{1} = 2{F}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}\left(1 + \mu\right) = 2\dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}\left(1 - \mu\right)$

$⇒ 1 + \mu = 2 - 2\mu$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{1}{3} = 0 . 33$

questions.q: A body of mass $200g$ is tied to a spring of spring constant $12 . 5N{m}^{- 1}$, while the other end of spring is fixed at point $O$. If the body moves about $O$ in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed $5rad{s}^{- 1}$, then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be :
questions.solution:
Let the extension in spring be $x$ and the natural length of spring be $l$.

Here the centrifugal force will stretch the spring.

So, centrifugal force$=$spring force

$kx = m\left(l + x\right){\omega}^{2} ⇒ 12 . 5x = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(l + x\right)25 ⇒ 1 . 5x = l ⇒ \dfrac{x}{l} = \dfrac{1}{1 . 5} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ x: l = 2: 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: An elevator can go up or down with uniform speed when its weight is balanced with the tension of its cable.
Statement-II: Force exerted by the floor of an elevator on the foot of a person standing on it is more than his/her weight when the elevator goes down with increasing speed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.solution:
When elevator is moving with uniform speed $T = {F}_{g}$, as the net force along the vertical direction should be zero.

Therefore, Statement-I is true.

Now, when elevator is going down with increasing speed, its acceleration is downward.
Hence,

$W - N = ma ⇒ W - N = \dfrac{W}{g} \times a$

$⇒ N = W\left(1 - \dfrac{a}{g}\right)$

Clearly, normal reaction is less than weight. So Statement-II is false.

questions.q: A tube of length $50cm$ is filled completely with an incompressible liquid of mass $250g$ and closed at both ends. The tube is then rotated in horizontal plane about one of its ends with a uniform angular velocity $x\sqrt{F}rad{s}^{- 1}$. If $F$ be the force exerted by the liquid at the other end then the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.solution:
Considering an element of tube of length $d x$ having mass $d m$ at a distance of $x$ from right end as shown in figure below.

Now, force acting of that element is $F = ∫ \left(d m\right){\omega}^{2}x$

Integrating the above relation for whole length of tube, we have

$F = {∫}_{0}^{L}\left(\dfrac{m}{L} d x\right){\omega}^{2}x$

$= \dfrac{m}{L}{\omega}^{2}\dfrac{{L}^{2}}{2}$= \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}L}{2}$

$⇒ \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{mL}}\sqrt{F}$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{0 . 25 \times 0 . 5}}\sqrt{F}$

$= \sqrt{16}\sqrt{F}$= 4\sqrt{F}rad{s}^{- 1}$

Hence, the value of $x = 4$.

questions.q: A uniform metal chain of mass $m$ and length $L$ passes over a massless and frictionless pulley. It is released from rest with a part of its length $l$ is hanging on one side and rest of its length $L - l$ is hanging on the other side of the pulley. questions.solution:
According to the information given in the question, the part of the chain that envelopes the pulley is very small. Therefore, the acceleration of the chain can be written as,

$a = \dfrac{\left({m}_{2} - {m}_{1}\right)}{\left({m}_{2} + {m}_{1}\right)}g$

Since $a = \dfrac{g}{2}$

$\dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{\left({m}_{2} - {m}_{1}\right)}{\left({m}_{2} + {m}_{1}\right)}g ⇒ \dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{\left(L - l\right) - l}{L}g ⇒ l = \dfrac{L}{4} = \dfrac{L}{x}$

$⇒ x = 4$

questions.solution:
As per the information given in the question the lift is moving upward with uniform velocity. Therefore, the frame of reference attached to the lift is an inertial frame of reference. The acceleration of the block down the incline will be,

$a = gsin\theta$

Using equation of motion for constant acceleration,

$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{1}{2}gsin30 ° {\left(2\right)}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

When the inclination is changed to $45 °$,

$l = \dfrac{1}{2}gsin45 ° {t}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equating the above equations,

When the bag is dropped on the conveyor belt, the acceleration of the bag will be $a = \mug = 4m{s}^{- 2}$

Using the equation of motion for constant acceleration,

${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$

$⇒ s = 0 . 5m$

questions.q: A monkey of mass $50kg$ climbs on a rope which can withstand the tension $\left(T\right) of 350N$. If monkey initially climbs down with an acceleration of $4m{s}^{- 2}$ and then climbs up with an acceleration of $5m{s}^{- 2}$. Choose the correct option $\left(g = 10m{s}^{- 2}\right)$
options: Rope will break while climbing upward
Rope will break while going downward
questions.solution:
Let ${a}_{1}$ be the acceleration of monkey while moving down.

F.B.D of monkey while moving downward

Using Newton's second law of motion,

$mg - T = m{a}_{1}$

$∴ 500 - T = 50 \times 4 ⇒ T = 300N$

Let ${a}_{2}$ be the acceleration of monkey while moving up.

F.B.D of monkey while moving up

Using Newton's second law of motion

$T - mg = m{a}_{2}$

$⇒ T - 500 = 50 \times 5$

$⇒ T = 750N$

Breaking strength of rope $= 750 - 300 = 350N$

$∴$ Rope will break while monkey is moving upward.

questions.q: For a free body diagram shown in the figure, the four forces are applied in the '$x$' and '$y$' directions. What additional force must be applied and at what angle with positive $x$-axis so that the net acceleration of body is zero?
questions.solution:
Let additional force required be $\overset{\to}{F}$.

Vector sum of the four forces and additional force.

$\overset{\to}{F} + 5\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{j} = 0$

Force required to make net acceleration zero

$\overset{\to}{F} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

Therefore, the required force is $\left|\overset{\to}{F}\right| = \sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{2}N$

Angle with $x$-axis: $tan\theta = \dfrac{ycomponent}{xcomponent} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

Thus, $\theta = 45 °$

questions.q: A block of mass $2kg$ moving on a horizontal surface with speed of $4{ms}^{- 1}$ enters a rough surface ranging from $x = 0 . 5m$ to $x = 1 . 5m$. The retarding force in this range of rough surface is related to distance by $F = - kx$ where $k = 12N{m}^{- 1}$. The speed of the block as it just crosses the rough surface will be
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the block $a = \dfrac{f}{m} = - \dfrac{12x}{2} = - 6x$ (Here the block is retarding)

Now, using, $a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$
$⇒ vdv = adx$
On integrating, we get

${∫}_{4}^{v}v d v = - 6{∫}_{0 . 5}^{1 . 5}x d x$

$⇒ \dfrac{{v}^{2} - {4}^{2}}{2} = - 6\left(\dfrac{{\left(1 . 5\right)}^{2} - {\left(0 . 5\right)}^{2}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = 16 - 12 ⇒ v = 2m{s}^{- 1}$

Neglect mass of the string and friction of the block (bigger mass) with ice slab.
(Given $g =$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
Equation for $4M: 2Mg - T = 4Ma . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation for $M: T - Mg = Ma . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding both equation we get,

$Mg = 5Ma ⇒ a = \dfrac{g}{5}$

Now, tension $T = Mg + Ma = \dfrac{6Mg}{5}$

Therefore, $x = 6$

questions.q: One end of a massless spring of spring constant $k$ and natural length ${l}_{0}$ is fixed while the other end is connected to a small object of mass $m$ lying on a frictionless table. The spring remains horizontal on the table. If the object is made to rotate at an angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis passing trough fixed end, then the elongation of the spring will be
questions.solution:
The particle is moving in a horizontal circle, so it is accelerated towards the centre with magnitude $\dfrac{{v}^{2}}{r}$. The horizontal force on the particle is due to the spring and is given by $kx$, where $x$ is the elongation and $k$ is the spring constant.

$kx = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{r} = m{\omega}^{2}r = m{\omega}^{2}\left({l}_{0} + x\right)$

$⇒ \left(k - m{\omega}^{2}\right)x = m{\omega}^{2}{l}_{0}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}{l}_{0}}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}$

questions.q: A curved in a level road has a radius $75m$. The maximum speed of a car turning this curved road can be $30m{s}^{- 1}$ without skidding. If radius of curved road is changed to $48m$ and the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road remains same, then maximum allowed speed would be _____  $m{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
The maximum speed is given as $v = \sqrt{\mugr}$, where, $\mu$ is coefficient of friction and $r$ is radius of curved road.

$⇒ \dfrac{30}{{v}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{75}{48}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{16}} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = 24m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A uniform chain of $6m$ length is placed on a table such that a part of its length is hanging over the edge of the table. The system is at rest. The co-efficient of static friction between the chain and the surface of the table is $0 . 5$, the maximum length of the chain hanging from the table is _____ $m$.
questions.solution:
Let, $\lambda =$mass per unit length of the chain and length of mass hanging through the table is $x$.

Normal force applied by the table on the chain will be, $N = \left(l - x\right)\lambdag$.

Tension developed in the chain will balance the gravitational force acting in the downward direction, $T = \lambdaxg$.

Maximum limiting force possible for the part of the table, ${f}_{max} = \muN = \mu\left(l - x\right)\lambdag$

For equilibrium,

${f}_{max} = T$,

$⇒ \mu\left(l - x\right)\lambdag = \lambdaxg ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(6 - x\right) = x ⇒ x = 2m$

questions.q: The normal reaction $N$ for a vehicle of $800kg$ mass, negotiating a turn on a $30 °$ banked road at maximum possible speed without skidding is ____ $\times {10}^{3}kgm{s}^{- 2}$.

At ${v}_{max}, f$ will be limiting in nature.

Hence, option $1 .$

It is desired to make the body move by applying the minimum possible force $FN$. The value of $F$ will be _______.(Round off to the Nearest Integer) [Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$ ]

$Fcos\theta = \muN$

$⇒ Fsin\theta + N = mg$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{\mumg}{cos\theta + \musin\theta}$

At maximum ht. block will experience maximum friction force. Therefore if at this height slope of the tangent is $tan\theta,$ then $\theta =$Angle of repose

$⇒ x = 1$ and therefore $y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} = 0 . 25m$

$= 25cm$

$∴$ Answer is $25cm$

(Assuming that $x$ & $y$ in the equation are given in meter)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is fixed to one end of a light spring having force constant $k$ and unstretched length $l .$ The other end is fixed. The system is given an angular speed $\omega$ about the fixed end of the spring such that it rotates in a circle in gravity free space. Then the stretch in the spring is:
questions.solution:
As we know, the spring force will give the necessary centripetal force for rotation.

So,

$m{\omega}^{2}\left(l + x\right) = kx$
$\left(\dfrac{l}{x} + 1\right) = \dfrac{k}{m{\omega}^{2}}$

Thus, the stretch in the spring
$x = \dfrac{lm{\omega}^{2}}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}$

A force $F$ is applied horizontally at the mid-point of the rope such that the top half of the rope makes an angle of $45 °$ with the vertical. Then $F$ equals: (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$ and the rope to be massless)
questions.solution:
Let the tension in the string is $T$.

Applying the condition of equilibrium in the vertical direction,

$Tcos\left(45 °\right) = 100$

$⇒ \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} = 100 . . . \left(1\right)$

In the horizontal direction,

$Tsin\left(45 °\right) = F$

$⇒ \dfrac{T}{\sqrt{2}} = F$

Put the value of $T$ from equation $\left(1\right)$,

$⇒ F = 100N$

So, the horizontal force applied on the rope will be $100N$.

$∴ {\left(100\dfrac{b}{a}\right)}_{max} = 50.00$

Net force on ball,

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{mg}{A} = {P}_{2}$

$= \dfrac{nRT}{g}\left(\dfrac{{l}_{1} - {l}_{2}}{{l}_{1}{l}_{2}}\right)$

questions.q: A particle of mass $\mathrm{m}$ is moving in a straight line with momentum p. Starting at time $t=0,$ a force $F=k$ t acts in the same direction on the moving particle during time interval T so that its momentum changes from $\mathrm{p}$ to $3 \mathrm{p}$. Here $k$ is a constant. The value of $\mathrm{T}$ is
questions.solution:
From Newton's second law

$\frac{\mathrm{dp}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{kt}$

Integrating both sides we get, $\int_{\mathrm{p}}^{3 \mathrm{p}} \mathrm{dp}=\int_{0}^{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{ktdt} \Rightarrow[\mathrm{p}]_{\mathrm{p}}^{3 \mathrm{p}}=\mathrm{k}\left[\frac{\mathrm{t}^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{\mathrm{T}}$\Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{kT}^{2}}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=2 \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{k}}}$

questions.q: A large number $( n )$ of identical beads, each of mass $m$ and radius $r$ are strung on a thin smooth rigid horizontal rod of length $L ( L ≫ r )$ and are at rest at random positions. The rod is mounted between two rigid supports (see figure). If one of the beads is now given a speed $v$, the average force experienced by each support after a long time is (assume all collisions are elastic):
questions.solution:
Average time for $1$ collision to occur on $1$ wall,~
$= {t}_{avg} = \dfrac{averagedistancetravelled}{speed}= \dfrac{2\left(L - 2nr\right)}{v}$

$⇒ {t}_{avg} = \dfrac{2\left(L - 2nr\right)}{v}$. Change in momentum in~$1$ collision $= 2mv$. Average force on each support,~${f}_{avg} = \dfrac{2mv}{tavg} = \dfrac{2mv^{2}}{2\left(L - 2nr\right)}⇒ {f}_{avg} = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{L - 2nr}$.

${F}_{B}cos 60 ° = \mu\left(mg - {F}_{B}sin60 °\right)$

we get,

questions.q: A bullet of mass $4 \mathrm{~g}$ is fired horizontally with a speed of $300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ into $0.8 \mathrm{~kg}$ block of wood at rest on a table. If the coefficient of friction between the block and the table is $0.3$, how far will the block slide approximately?
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathrm{m}_1=4 \mathrm{~g}, \mathrm{u}_1=300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\mathrm{m}_2=0.8 \mathrm{~kg}=800 \mathrm{~g}, \mathrm{u}_2=0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ From law of conservation of momentum, $\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{u}_1+\mathrm{m}_2 \mathrm{u}_2=\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{m}_2 \mathrm{v}_2$ Let the velocity of combined system $=\mathrm{v} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ then, $4 \times 300+800 \times 0=(800+4) \times v\mathrm{v}=\frac{1200}{804}=1.49 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Now, $\mu=0.3$ (given)

$\begin{aligned}$&$\mathrm{a}=\mu \mathrm{g}$\\
&$\mathrm{a}=$0.3 $\times$10$\left(\text{ take } \mathrm{g}=$10 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^$2\right) \\
&=3 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^$2
\end{aligned}

then,$ from \mathrm{v}^2=\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{as}$
(1.49)^2=0+2 $\times$3 $\times$s

$\mathrm{s}=\frac{\left(1.49^2\right)}{6} ; \mathrm{s}=\frac{2.22}{6}=0.379 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{F}_0 \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{bt}} \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}_0}{\mathrm{~m}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{bt}} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}_0}{\mathrm{~m}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{bt}} \quad\int \mathrm{dv}=\int_0^{\mathrm{t}} \frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{bt}} \mathrm{dt} \Rightarrow v=\frac{F}{m}\left[\frac{-1}{b}\right]\left[e^{-b t}\right]_0^t \Rightarrow \quad v=\frac{F}{m b}\left[e^{-b t}\right] v=0 \text{ at } t=0$ and $\quad v \rightarrow \frac{F}{m b}$ as $t \rightarrow \infty$
So, velocity increases continuously and attains a maximum value of $v=\frac{F}{m b}$ as $t \rightarrow \infty$.
